hero.caption:
Housing, Fort Lawton, Seattle, Washington. This housing in the "600 area" (13 units are on a 5.5 acre parcel in a historic district with views of Puget Sound ) is still in use as Naval officers' housing as of 2007, but will soon be converted to non-military use [which has happened, as of 2022]. [1]< br/>
Fort Lawton is on the National Register of Historic Places.

images.caption:
Disused buildings of Fort Lawton, Seattle, Washington seen from the Henry M. Jackson Viewpoint. These buildings in the "600 area" are, left to right, the Post Exchange/Gymnasium and the Band and Barracks. In the distance at right is U.S. Navy housing still in use; I believe it's the "Capeheart" site, which will soon be leveled and made part of Discovery Park, as part of the ongoing conversion of Fort Lawton into that park. [1]

Fort Lawton is on the National Register of Historic Places.

images.filename: Aerial view of Discovery Park and Fort Lawton in Seattle.jpg
images.caption: Aerial view of Magnolia peninsular neighborhood in Seattle, facing north north west. Left is Puget Sound, center right is Lake Washington Ship Canal, top right is Ballard.
